name: Bánh căn
summary: Bite-size rice cakes grilled over charcoal, with a quail egg or a duck egg on top. At Lệ the shell is crisp, and one dip is an onion sauce.
origin: A Da Lat cake in the line of Hue bánh bèo, grilled over a charcoal brazier.
texture: The cakes are bite-size. At Bánh Căn Lệ the shell is crisp.
howToEat: Eat them early, as breakfast or a light snack, with a quail egg or a duck egg on the cake. One account dips them in onion sauce.

Fillings change by door. Cây Bơ sets out quail egg, chicken egg, meat, shrimp, or a soft-yolk egg, with mắm nêm or xíu mại sauce. Lệ sets out minced beef, quail egg, chicken egg, or seafood, with fish sauce or mắm nêm, and a crisp shell. The door called Bánh căn Đà Lạt sets out quail egg, minced beef, or chicken egg, with xíu mại sauce and fish sauce. A Cát sets out chicken egg, chicken with beef, quail egg, quail egg with beef, seafood, chicken with squid, or quail egg with oyster, plus xíu mại and pickled vegetables.
where: The centre, especially around Hoa Binh.

56 Tăng Bạt Hổ, open 06:00–11:30. 7 Tăng Bạt Hổ, open 16:00–23:00. 27/44 Yersin, open 06:00–19:00. A Cát is at H55 KQH Nguyễn Thị Nghĩa, also written H54-55, with 08:00–23:59 in the header and 07:00–21:30 in the text.
priceBand: Visit Lâm Đồng prints 15,000–30,000 VND at Cây Bơ and at Lệ, 20,000–50,000 VND at 7 Tăng Bạt Hổ, and “Đang cập nhật” at A Cát. Cây Bơ also prints 30,000 VND for five pairs, and Lệ’s text says 25,000 VND. Vietnam Tourism prints no price. A single city price is Check on arrival.
